mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Negative 3-month FEDFUNDS change is followed by negative 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of historical instances.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The unemployment rate rises above 4.0% but the subsequent 5-day S&P 500 return is positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both housing starts (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening in aggregate demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day S&P 500 return is positive in more than 60% of the periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by more than 1% from their 3-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO), manufacturing output contraction leads to reduced corporate profits and negative equity returns, with the effect being most pronounced in the first 20 trading days after the decline is observed.
failure_condition: The 20-day S&P 500 return is positive in more than 60% of the periods when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% over the past 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer spending index (RSAFS) indicates strong household demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day S&P 500 return is negative in more than 60% of the periods when RSAFS rises by more than 0.5% from the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annually signals accelerating inflation, which prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day S&P 500 return is positive in more than 60% of the periods when CPIAUCSL rises above 2.5% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in unemployment (UNRATE) and decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day S&P 500 return is positive in more than 60% of the periods when UNRATE rises and PAYEMS declines by more than 0.5% from the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year), the Federal Reserve's tightening response leads to negative equity returns, with the effect being most pronounced over a 60-day horizon.
failure_condition: The 60-day S&P 500 return is positive in more than 60% of the periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% year-over-year.
